text.short: Bakersfield, 1901. A boarding house by the rail yard that never stopped feeding people.
text.today: It opens for breakfast, which almost no Basque dining room does, and runs through to a late bar.
text.history: It went up near the Bakersfield train station in 1901 and took in Basque men who arrived by rail and left for the hills with a flock. The boarders are gone; the long tables stayed.

x_kitchen.says: Basque, out of a boarding house

founded.note: Other accounts put the house at 1899; the café's own site says 1901.

seating.note: Long tables, dishes passed. Call ahead and the house will seat you.

picon.note: The bar runs until 9 or 10 most nights; the site does not print a drink list.

hours.text: Mon and Wed 8am–9pm · Tue dining to 3pm, bar to 9pm · Thu–Fri 8am–10pm · Sat 7am–10pm · Sun 7am–9pm
